FIB_PLUS	<p>15b3_501e</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9d3724;">Gene E</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #9d3724;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9d3724;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #286f21;">Gene J</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #286f21;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #286f21;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #256682;">Gene K</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #256682;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #256682;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ejk, +++, ejk"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. FIB_PLUS	<p>3721_eada</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7d550c;">Gene P</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #7d550c;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7d550c;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #236d4f;">Gene W</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #236d4f;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #236d4f;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7d4092;">Gene Y</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #7d4092;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. FIB_PLUS	<p>de1b_427f</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #286f21;">Gene M</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #286f21;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #286f21;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #256682;">Gene N</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #256682;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #256682;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8f3974;">Gene T</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #8f3974;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. FIB_PLUS	<p>c63b_b76f</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7d550c;">Gene B</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #7d550c;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7d550c;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a76;">Gene M</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006a76;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. map distance between the two genes.</li> <ul><li>D = &half; (TT + 6 NPD) / total = (3 NPD + &half; TT) / total</li></ul> <li>Step 5: Go back to Step 2 and pick a new pair of genes until all pairs are Finding a decimal in your answer, such as 5.5, indicates a mistake was made. Please provide your answer as a complete number without fractions or decimals.</li><li><i>Important Tip 2:</i> Your answer should be written as a numerical value only, with no spaces, commas, or units such as "cM" or "map units". FIB_PLUS	<p>eb80_bbc9</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #57660b;">Gene C</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #57660b;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #57660b;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a76;">Gene M</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006a76;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a76;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8f3974;">Gene T</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #8f3974;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6d5d0b;">Gene B</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #6d5d0b;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6d5d0b;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #0961a4;">Gene K</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #0961a4;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0961a4;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8f3974;">Gene Y</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #8f3974;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. FIB_PLUS	<p>e9d2_5643</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9d3724;">Gene C</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #9d3724;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9d3724;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #286f21;">Gene K</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #286f21;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #286f21;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #0961a4;">Gene M</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #0961a4;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0961a4;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ckm, +++, ckm"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. FIB_PLUS	<p>40d4_c83e</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #286f21;">Gene J</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #286f21;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #286f21;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #256682;">Gene T</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #256682;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #256682;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8f3974;">Gene Y</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #8f3974;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8f3974;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, jty, +++, jty"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. FIB_PLUS	<p>54f3_9593</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7d550c;">Gene A</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #7d550c;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7d550c;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #256682;">Gene W</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #256682;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #256682;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8f3974;">Gene Y</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #8f3974;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8f3974;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, awy, +++, awy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9d3724;">Gene B</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #9d3724;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9d3724;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #286f21;">Gene H</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #286f21;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #286f21;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4456ab;">Gene P</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #4456ab;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #286f21;">Gene H</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #286f21;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #286f21;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #256682;">Gene N</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #256682;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. FIB_PLUS	<p>a002_65fc</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6d5d0b;">Gene B</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #6d5d0b;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6d5d0b;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d64;">Gene H</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006d64;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d64;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8f3974;">Gene X</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #8f3974;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. FIB_PLUS	<p>15b4_885b</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #57660b;">Gene D</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #57660b;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #57660b;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a76;">Gene N</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006a76;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a76;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8f3974;">Gene X</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #8f3974;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9d3724;">Gene F</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #9d3724;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6d5d0b;">Gene B</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #6d5d0b;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6d5d0b;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #256682;">Gene P</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #256682;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #256682;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7d4092;">Gene T</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #7d4092;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. FIB_PLUS	<p>28d1_2bf2</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8d4912;">Gene D</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #8d4912;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8d4912;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #236d4f;">Gene N</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #236d4f;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #236d4f;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #0961a4;">Gene X</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #0961a4;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. FIB_PLUS	<p>8767_dafe</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7d550c;">Gene A</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #7d550c;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7d550c;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #236d4f;">Gene E</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #236d4f;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #236d4f;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #0961a4;">Gene F</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #0961a4;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. FIB_PLUS	<p>4b93_5664</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #57660b;">Gene H</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #57660b;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #57660b;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a76;">Gene P</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006a76;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a76;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9e2f4e;">Gene W</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #9e2f4e;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. FIB_PLUS	<p>8048_ceea</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8d4912;">Gene C</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #8d4912;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8d4912;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #286f21;">Gene K</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #286f21;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #286f21;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4456ab;">Gene P</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #4456ab;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. FIB_PLUS	<p>68e0_b72a</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9d3724;">Gene D</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #9d3724;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9d3724;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #236d4f;">Gene P</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #236d4f;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #236d4f;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6547ae;">Gene Y</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #6547ae;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. FIB_PLUS	<p>e5e5_2540</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6d5d0b;">Gene C</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #6d5d0b;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6d5d0b;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a76;">Gene H</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006a76;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a76;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8f3974;">Gene W</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #8f3974;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9d3724;">Gene E</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #9d3724;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9d3724;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #57660b;">Gene H</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #57660b;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #57660b;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6547ae;">Gene P</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #6547ae;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. FIB_PLUS	<p>de5b_c421</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #286f21;">Gene N</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #286f21;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #286f21;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #0961a4;">Gene X</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #0961a4;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. genes.</li> <li>Step 2: Pick any two genes and assign PD, NPD, TT.</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul> <li>Step 4: Determine the map distance between the two genes.</li> <ul><li>D = &half; (TT + 6 NPD) / total = (3 NPD + &half; TT) / total</li></ul> <li>Step 5: Go back to Step 2 and whole number. Finding a decimal in your answer, such as 5.5, indicates a mistake was made. Please provide your answer as a complete number without fractions or decimals.</li><li><i>Important Tip 2:</i> Your answer should be written as a numerical value only, with no spaces, commas, or units such as "cM" or "map units". FIB_PLUS	<p>fe68_03d1</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6d5d0b;">Gene E</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #6d5d0b;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6d5d0b;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d64;">Gene H</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006d64;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d64;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9e2f4e;">Gene W</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #9e2f4e;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. FIB_PLUS	<p>659a_1afb</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8d4912;">Gene K</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #8d4912;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8d4912;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #236d4f;">Gene P</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #236d4f;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #236d4f;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6547ae;">Gene X</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #6547ae;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype.
